title: atoll conflicts resolve <path> --keep <disk> --json
description: What keeping one copy of a file in conflict did, or would do with --yes: the copy kept first, then the others by disk position, each to the trash (specs.md §15.7). Exit 0 once the file is resolved, and with --dry-run; 3 when there is something to do and no --yes; 4 when a copy stayed, so the file is still in conflict; and 1, with nothing on standard output, when the catalog has no file at the path, the file is not in conflict, or it has no copy on that disk.

keep.description: The disk whose copy is kept.

applied.description: Whether it was allowed to write: --yes.

resolved.description: The file is no longer in conflict: every other copy went to the trash, and the next pass makes its copies from the one kept.

bytes.description: The sizes of the copies to-trash or trashed.

outcome.description: The copy kept, as its disk holds it now: kept; or gone, no longer there, or disk-unavailable, and then nothing moves and every other copy is not-moved. Any other copy: to-trash without --yes, trashed with it, gone when no longer on its disk, which removes its row, or why it stayed: disk-unavailable, changed between the look and the move, name-refused or io-error.
